rationale: Switching from haloperidol decanoate (long-acting depot) to oral haloperidol. Haloperidol decanoate has a t½ of ~21 days (range 14–35 days) and continues releasing for 6–8 weeks after the last injection. Start oral haloperidol when the next depot injection would have been due; the decanoate provides a natural taper. The oral/depot dose equivalence is approximately 1:10–15 (mg daily oral : mg decanoate per 4 weeks). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Skip the next scheduled decanoate injection. Start oral haloperidol 2 mg/day. Decanoate continues releasing — monitor for combined effect, particularly EPS.
Decanoate level declining. Increase oral haloperidol to 5 mg/day. Monitor EPS (akathisia, parkinsonism) and clinical state.
Decanoate substantially cleared (~6 weeks). Oral haloperidol 5 mg/day approaching sole therapeutic agent.
Decanoate cleared (~2 months). Oral haloperidol 5 mg/day monotherapy. Adjust 2–10 mg based on clinical response. Consider anticholinergic cover for EPS.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Haloperidol decanoate 50 mg/month ≈ oral haloperidol 5 mg/day (Maudsley 15th; ratio ~1:10). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

safetyFlags.title: EPS risk (FGA)
safetyFlags.body: Haloperidol is a high-potency FGA with significant EPS risk. Ensure anticholinergic prophylaxis is available. Monitor for akathisia, parkinsonism, and tardive dyskinesia.

safetyFlags.title: ECG / QTc
safetyFlags.body: Haloperidol prolongs QTc. Obtain baseline ECG and monitor, especially at higher doses.

safetyFlags.title: Decanoate tail
safetyFlags.body: Haloperidol decanoate t½ ~21 days. Therapeutic levels persist 6–8 weeks after the last injection. Start oral dose conservatively.
